scope: R24/R25 complete videos were encoded and decoded. Visual inspection covered eight full-trajectory storyboards at 15-step spacing and every one of the 77 free-release frames. This is not a claim that every held-phase frame was visually inspected.

observations: Local grasp indentation, traction of the pedicle, first partial cut and separation on the second cut remain visible.
No baseline-like pointed collapse during free release in the reviewed frames.
Repeated small bounces after contact, followed by sliding toward the back; the piece is still partly visible at step 1320.
cases.limitation: Surface grouping was incorrectly used as true-cut contact identity; R24 is diagnostic only.

observations: The initial grasp, traction and blade compression are similar in gross shape to the retained baseline and R24.
The second snip separates the tissue; the held piece relaxes after separation. No straight-line wound construction was added.

Free release reaches the organ surface without the baseline-like pointed collapse. Repeated small bounces and subsequent backward sliding remain visible; the piece is still partly visible at step 1320.
cases.limitation: This fixture uses inherited assisted contact model 2 before release. It does not validate pure-friction grasping or clinical realism.
